recommended_approach: Use Mantaflow’s liquid simulation settings via the Fluid Domain and Flow property groups: configure a Liquid Domain and drive the “FLIP-ness” of the solver through `bpy.types.FluidDomainSettings.flip_ratio`, then feed the domain with an inflow object whose motion/variation can be shaped using `bpy.types.FluidFlowSettings` (including a `noise_texture`). This aligns with the Python API structure where liquid/FLIP behavior is exposed on `FluidDomainSettings` (e.g., `flip_ratio`) and flow/emitter modulation is exposed on `FluidFlowSettings` (e.g., `noise_texture`).

key_parameters.FluidDomainSettings.flip_ratio: Documented as an attribute on `bpy.types.FluidDomainSettings` (see genindex entry for `flip_ratio`). This is the key FLIP vs PIC control exposed in the API; use it as the primary knob for splashy/energetic liquid behavior.
key_parameters.FluidDomainSettings.noise_strength: Documented as an attribute on `bpy.types.FluidDomainSettings` (see genindex entry for `noise_strength`).
key_parameters.FluidDomainSettings.noise_time_anim: Documented as an attribute on `bpy.types.FluidDomainSettings` (see genindex entry for `noise_time_anim`).
key_parameters.FluidDomainSettings.noise_type: Documented as an attribute on `bpy.types.FluidDomainSettings` (see genindex entry for `noise_type`).
key_parameters.FluidFlowSettings.noise_texture: Documented as an attribute on `bpy.types.FluidFlowSettings` (see genindex entry showing `noise_texture (bpy.types.FluidFlowSettings attribute)`). Useful for adding controlled variation to an inflow/stream.
